_source: Finance Bill 2025, Bill No. 14 of 2025, as introduced in Lok Sabha on 1st February 2025
_auditNote: Slabs extracted verbatim from First Schedule (Paragraph A, Part III) and Section 115BAC of Finance Bill 2025. New regime table (clause 24, pages 152-153 of Bill) and Section 87A amendment (clause 20, page 149) take effect from 1st April 2026 (AY 2026-27). This file covers FY 2025-26 (AY 2025-26) rates only.
_effectiveYearWarning: The 7-slab new regime (0/5/10/15/20/25/30% on 4L/8L/12L/16L/20L/24L boundaries) and 87A rebate of Rs 60,000 up to Rs 12L income are AY 2026-27 changes. FY 2025-26 uses the prior 6-slab new regime with 87A rebate of Rs 25,000 up to Rs 7L.

oldRegime.name: Old Tax Regime
oldRegime._source: Finance Bill 2025, First Schedule, Part III, Paragraph A, Item (I) — applicable for AY 2025-26

slabs.description: Income up to Rs. 2,50,000 — Nil (Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(I)(1))
Rs. 2,50,000 to Rs. 5,00,000 — 5% (Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(I)(2))
Rs. 5,00,000 to Rs. 10,00,000 — 20% (Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(I)(3))

seniorCitizenSlabs.description: Up to Rs. 3,00,000 — Nil (Resident 60-79, Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(II))

superSeniorCitizenSlabs.description: Up to Rs. 5,00,000 — Nil (Resident 80+, Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(III))

surcharge._source: Finance Bill 2025, First Schedule, Paragraph A, Surcharge provisions (pages 101-103)

thresholds.description: 10% surcharge — income > Rs. 50L but <= Rs. 1Cr (Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(a))
15% surcharge — income > Rs. 1Cr but <= Rs. 2Cr (Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(b))
25% surcharge — income > Rs. 2Cr but <= Rs. 5Cr (Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(c))
37% surcharge — income > Rs. 5Cr (Finance Bill 2025, Paragraph A(d))

surcharge._marginalReliefNote: Marginal relief applies at each threshold band per Finance Bill 2025 provisos under Paragraph A surcharge

oldRegime._cessNote: 4% Health and Education Cess on income-tax + surcharge (unchanged, not amended by Finance Bill 2025)

rebate87A._source: Section 87A of Income-tax Act, 1961 (NOT amended by Finance Bill 2025 for AY 2025-26)
rebate87A._note: Finance Bill 2025 Clause 20 amends 87A but takes effect from 1st April 2026 (AY 2026-27). For AY 2025-26, the existing provision applies.
rebate87A.description: Rebate under Section 87A — max Rs. 12,500 for income up to Rs. 5,00,000 (pre-amendment, applicable AY 2025-26)

section80C.description: LIC, PPF, ELSS, NSC, Home Loan Principal, Tuition Fees, Sukanya Samriddhi etc. — max Rs. 1,50,000

section80CCD1B._source: Section 80CCD(1B) — NPS additional contribution over and above 80C. Finance Bill 2025 Clause 17 extends to NPS Vatsalya accounts (minors) effective AY 2026-27 only.
section80CCD1B.description: Additional NPS contribution — max Rs. 50,000 (over and above 80C limit)

section80D.description: Health insurance premiums — self/family: Rs. 25,000 (Rs. 50,000 if senior); parents: Rs. 25,000 (Rs. 50,000 if senior)

section80E.description: Interest on education loan — no upper limit

section80G.description: Donations to approved charitable institutions — 50% or 100% depending on institution

standardDeduction.description: Standard deduction for salaried employees — Rs. 50,000

hra.description: HRA exemption under Rule 2A — minimum of: actual HRA, rent paid minus 10% basic, 50%/40% of basic (metro/non-metro)

newRegime.name: New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC)
newRegime._source: Section 115BAC(1A) of Income-tax Act as it stands for AY 2025-26. Finance Bill 2025 Clause 24 amends this table but takes effect from 1st April 2026 (AY 2026-27).
newRegime._applicableSlabTable: The 6-slab table below applies for AY 2025-26 (FY 2025-26). The 7-slab table introduced by Finance Bill 2025 Clause 24 applies from AY 2026-27 onwards.

surcharge._source: Same surcharge structure as old regime — Finance Bill 2025 does not change new regime surcharge rates for AY 2025-26

rebate87A._source: Finance Bill 2025 Clause 20 (page 149) — amends 87A proviso: replaces Rs. 7,00,000 with Rs. 12,00,000 and Rs. 25,000 with Rs. 60,000. EFFECTIVE DATE: 1st April 2026 (AY 2026-27). For AY 2025-26, prior values apply.
rebate87A.description: Rebate under Section 87A (New Regime) — max Rs. 25,000 for income up to Rs. 7,00,000 (pre-amendment, AY 2025-26)
rebate87A._marginalReliefNote: If taxable income > Rs. 7L and tax liability > (income - 7L), rebate = tax - (income - 7L) per existing proviso (b)

standardDeduction.description: Standard deduction for salaried employees — Rs. 50,000 (only deduction allowed in new regime)

newRegime_AY2026_27._note: These are the FUTURE rules effective from AY 2026-27 per Finance Bill 2025. Do NOT use for FY 2025-26 calculations.
newRegime_AY2026_27._source: Finance Bill 2025 Clause 24 (Section 115BAC amendment, pages 152-153) and Clause 20 (Section 87A amendment, page 149) — effective 1st April 2026

slabs.description: Up to Rs. 4,00,000 — Nil (Finance Bill 2025 Clause 24, AY 2026-27)

rebate87A.description: Rebate under Section 87A (New Regime, AY 2026-27) — max Rs. 60,000 for income up to Rs. 12,00,000

section44AD._source: Section 44AD, Income-tax Act 1961. Finance Bill 2025 does not amend Section 44AD threshold for AY 2025-26.
section44AD._note: Threshold is Rs. 2 crore for businesses with cash receipts > 5% of total. Rs. 3 crore threshold (introduced by Finance Act 2023) applies only where cash receipts do not exceed 5% of total receipts.
section44AD.description: Presumptive taxation — 6% of digital receipts + 8% of cash receipts. Threshold: Rs. 2Cr (Rs. 3Cr if cash <= 5% of total)

section44ADA._source: Section 44ADA, Income-tax Act 1961. Finance Bill 2025 does not amend this for AY 2025-26.
section44ADA.description: Presumptive taxation for professionals — 50% of gross receipts. Threshold: Rs. 50L (Rs. 75L if cash <= 5% of total)
